items.claim: The messenger-frame onset is correctly owned in the bytes, but both of this span's seams sit on byte-true devices left undisclosed: the divine title stack repeats at byte tier from the verse immediately before the front seam, and the span's own closing verse opens with the in-that-day formula that this same stretch elsewhere treats as a unit-opening driver.
items.evidence: Frame ownership verifies: the quoted onset run matches the source bytes at byte tier at oshb:Isa.10.24, and the formula belongs to the divine-frame class (44 of the 48 formula verses) rather than the royal-messenger class (exactly 4 verses: MT 36:4, 36:14, 36:16, 37:3, all in the narrative zone) - that part of the argument holds. What is undisclosed is that the title stack it carries, אֲדֹנָ֤י יְהוִה֙ צְבָא֔וֹת (oshb:Isa.10.24, byte tier), is BYTE-IDENTICAL to the stack closing the preceding verse, אֲדֹנָ֤י יְהוִה֙ צְבָא֔וֹת (oshb:Isa.10.23, byte tier); this stack reaches 8 verses (sweep: 8 verses, MT keys Isa.3.15, 10:23, 10:24, 22:5, 22:12, 22:14, 22:15, 28:22), of which only two pairs are adjacent (MT 10:23|10:24 and MT 22:14|22:15) and this is one of them. The row cites the preceding verse solely for its paragraph mark and never engages this byte-tier carry-over across its own front seam, where a byte-true device straddling the seam argues continuity unless disclosed. Second, the span's final verse opens וְהָיָ֣ה בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא (oshb:Isa.10.27, byte tier), byte-identical to the same formula at oshb:Isa.10.20 and oshb:Isa.11.11 (sweep: 13 verses at skeleton tier, MT keys Isa.7.18, 7:21, 7:23, 10:20, 10:27, 11:10, 11:11, 17:4, 22:20, 23:15, 24:21, 27:12, 27:13); that formula is treated as a unit-opening driver at MT 10:20 and MT 11:10-11 in this same stretch, so its unit-internal occurrence at MT 10:27 needs disclosure or the formula's boundary force is asymmetric across neighbouring cuts. Parashah layer verifies clean: the setumah at MT 10:23 is the correct type, and no petuchah or setumah falls inside MT 10:24-27, so no symmetry debt is owed; one paseq seg stands at MT 10:27 (single-witness, count-only).

items.claim: The row leans on a ketiv/qere-bearing verse for its internal mark disclosure without any apparatus disclosure, and rests its closing device on a divine title whose Hebrew object it never names - one the English rendering flattens into the same words as the different stack quoted at the neighbouring seam.
items.evidence: Both quoted runs match the source bytes at byte tier, and the parashah claims verify with the correct type: setumah at MT 10:32 (inside the span) and setumah at MT 10:34 (at its close), with no petuchah in the span, so the never-conflate discipline holds. But MT 10:32 is a ketiv/qere verse (one note), staged as the doubled token pair inside הַ֣ר בית בַּת צִיּ֔וֹן (oshb:Isa.10.32, byte tier) - an unpointed ketiv beside its pointed qere - and the row argues from that very verse while making no apparatus disclosure; the book's ketiv/qere inventory runs to 53 notes over 49 verses and the check-before-slicing rule binds any span touching one of them. Second, the closing device quoted at oshb:Isa.10.33, הִנֵּ֤ה הָאָדוֹן֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת (byte tier), is the definite-article title stack, a count-object reaching 5 verses (sweep: 5 verses, MT keys Isa.1.24, 3:1, 10:16, 10:33, 19:4) - including MT 10:16, הָאָד֜וֹן יְהוָ֧ה צְבָא֛וֹת (oshb:Isa.10.16, byte tier), inside the immediately preceding stretch of this same chapter. It is a DIFFERENT object from אֲדֹנָ֤י יְהוִה֙ צְבָא֔וֹת (oshb:Isa.10.24, byte tier; sweep: 8 verses) quoted at the neighbouring seam, yet the English renders both identically, so neither the row's divine-title signal key nor its gloss distinguishes the two Hebrew stacks, and the in-chapter recurrence at MT 10:16 goes unengaged. Handling the place-name sequence as enumeration inside its unit rather than as a list register is correct, and disclosing the internal behold-seam candidate rather than passing it silently is the right register.

items.claim: The cut itself is well founded on the bytes, but both structural claims the row offers as its grounds - the stump image answering the felled trees across its front seam, and the closing inclusio - are asserted with no quoted Hebrew form and no tier label, and neither has a byte-level anchor.
items.evidence: The onset splice וְיָצָ֥א חֹ֖טֶר מִגֵּ֣זַע יִשָׁ֑י (oshb:Isa.11.1) matches the source bytes at byte tier, and the mark layer is right: setumah at MT 10:34, petuchah at MT 11:9, correct types, none inside MT 11:1-8, and no ketiv/qere note anywhere in the span, so nothing is owed there. The front-seam claim, however, supplies no Hebrew from the preceding side and has no lexical anchor there: the three growth nouns of MT 11:1 - חֹ֖טֶר (sweep: 1 verse), מִגֵּ֣זַע (sweep: 2 verses, MT 11:1 and 40:24) and וְנֵ֖צֶר (sweep: 5 verses) - share no root with the felling vocabulary of MT 10:33-34. As stated the link is a semantic continuity across the row's own seam, which under the cross-seam rule argues against the cut rather than for it, yet it is offered as boundary evidence. The closing inclusio names no bracketing term, quotes no form and labels no tier; the nearest byte candidate does not close at skeleton tier either, since MT 11:9's דֵּעָה֙ (oshb:Isa.11.9, byte tier; that skeleton reaches 8 verses) is not the form attested at MT 11:2, ר֥וּחַ דַּ֖עַת (oshb:Isa.11.2, byte tier; that skeleton reaches 26 verses). The back seam is sounder: the row discloses that the figure continues into the next verse, and the bytes carry that - מִשָּׁרָשָׁ֥יו (oshb:Isa.11.1, byte tier; sweep: 1 verse) and שֹׁ֣רֶשׁ יִשַׁ֗י (oshb:Isa.11.10, byte tier), the root reaching 9 verses at skeleton tier - though again without a quoted form or tier label in the row itself.

items.claim: The one-verse cut rests on an in-that-day formula that the immediately following verse repeats verse-initially at accent-stripped and skeleton tier, and on a second-time marker that is not that verse's opener, with a two-site banner catchword straddling the same seam undisclosed.
items.evidence: Both quoted runs match the source bytes at byte tier and both parashah claims verify with the correct type (petuchah at MT 11:9 and petuchah at MT 11:10), and the row rightly declines to treat them as drivers. The decisive problem is that the row's own driver recurs across its back seam: MT 11:10 opens וְהָיָה֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא and MT 11:11 opens וְהָיָ֣ה בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא (both oshb, byte tier) - identical at accent-stripped and skeleton tier, differing ONLY in accents, so not byte-identical, and the tier is named here because the row names none. That formula reaches 13 verses at skeleton tier (MT keys Isa.7.18, 7:21, 7:23, 10:20, 10:27, 11:10, 11:11, 17:4, 22:20, 23:15, 24:21, 27:12, 27:13) with the bare in-that-day core reaching 45, and four of its sites fall in this immediate stretch - one of them, MT 10:27, treated as unit-internal at a neighbouring cut. Neither the repetition nor its tier is disclosed. The distinguishing marker the row leans on is mid-verse, not an opener: שֵׁנִית֙ (oshb:Isa.11.11, byte tier; sweep: 2 verses, MT 11:11 and 37:30) stands as the sixth token of MT 11:11, after the shared formula, so the cut separates two verses whose verse-initial frames match while resting on a token that opens neither. A byte-attested catchword also straddles the seam undisclosed: the banner-noun at MT 11:10, עֹמֵד֙ לְנֵ֣ס עַמִּ֔ים (byte tier), and at MT 11:12, וְנָשָׂ֥א נֵס֙ לַגּוֹיִ֔ם (byte tier), that pairing reaching 2 verses (MT 5:26 and 11:12). The honest medium_low hold and the explicit statement that the verse could belong to either neighbour are the right register - it is the evidence layer, not the confidence label, that fails; separately, characterising one paragraph-break type as the more emphatic of the two is a scribal-convention assertion not sourced from the single-witness inventory the row cites.

items.claim: The run presented as what opens the unit is mid-verse, while the verse's actual opener is the same formula carrying the boundary at MT 11:10, and the row names only one of the two remnant-root objects that are live in the two verses it cites.
items.evidence: The quoted run matches the source bytes at byte tier, but it is not the verse's opening: the first three tokens of MT 11:11 are וְהָיָ֣ה בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא (oshb:Isa.11.11, byte tier) - byte-identical to the openers of MT 10:20 and MT 10:27 and identical at accent-stripped and skeleton tier to the opener of MT 11:10, the very verse this cut separates from - and יוֹסִ֨יף אֲדֹנָ֤י שֵׁנִית֙ (byte tier) begins only at the fourth token. Presenting it as what opens the unit misstates the byte position of the frame; the row's own rival disclosure concedes the shared in-that-day governance internally but never applies it to the seam. Remnant discipline: the row names the plain common-noun object at MT 11:11 and MT 11:16, but both verses also carry the survive-verb object - אֲשֶׁ֣ר יִשָּׁאֵר֩ (oshb:Isa.11.11, byte tier) and לִשְׁאָ֣ר עַמּ֔וֹ אֲשֶׁ֥ר יִשָּׁאֵ֖ר (oshb:Isa.11.16, byte tier), that verb form reaching exactly 2 verses (sweep: 2 verses, MT 11:11 and 11:16, both inside this span). Two of the root's four distinct objects sit in the same two verses and only one is named, and the unnamed one is part of the very noun-plus-relative construction the row treats as its closing echo. The divine name quoted at MT 11:11 is the bare form of the role-split census, quoted but never named as its own count-object. Mark and apparatus layers verify clean: petuchah at MT 11:10 correct type, no petuchah or setumah inside MT 11:11-16 (absence is never counterevidence), no ketiv/qere note in the span; a paseq pair stands at MT 11:11 (single-witness, count-only). The internal cohesion argument for holding MT 11:11-16 as one unit is itself byte-supported - the noun-plus-relative construction recurs at the span's two ends.

items.claim: The twin-onset recurrence claim holds at no Hebrew tier and is quoted only in English, its form-class gloss misnames the difference between the two speaking verbs, an addressee shift at the hymn's own last verse is contradicted rather than disclosed, and the span's ketiv/qere verse is left unchecked beneath a count claim.
items.evidence: MT 12:1 opens וְאָֽמַרְתָּ֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא and MT 12:4 opens וַאֲמַרְתֶּ֞ם בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא (both oshb, byte tier); each is a one-off in the book (sweep: 1 verse each) and the two are NOT identical at byte, accent-stripped, or skeleton tier - even the shared in-that-day core differs in accents between the two verses. The row quotes no Hebrew for either onset and labels no tier, so 'restates the same onset formula' stands on the English rendering alone; the genuinely shared object is the pervasive in-that-day core (sweep: 45 verses at skeleton tier, MT keys), which is not by itself a boundary or cohesion driver. The form-class gloss is wrong on the pointed bytes: וְאָֽמַרְתָּ֙ and וַאֲמַרְתֶּ֞ם (byte tier) are BOTH second person - only number differs, together with the conjunction vowel - so 'differs in person and number' is a byte-checkable claim that the bytes contest. Third, the row asserts that neither addressee nor register changes across the hymn, but MT 12:6 opens צַהֲלִ֥י וָרֹ֖נִּי יוֹשֶׁ֣בֶת צִיּ֑וֹן (byte tier) - a feminine-singular imperative pair with a feminine vocative, continued by the second-feminine-singular suffix בְּקִרְבֵּ֖ךְ (byte tier) - against the masculine-plural imperatives of MT 12:4 and MT 12:5, הוֹד֤וּ לַֽיהוָה֙ קִרְא֣וּ and זַמְּר֣וּ (byte tier); the same feminine imperative governs a feminine addressee at MT 10:30, צַהֲלִ֥י קוֹלֵ֖ךְ בַּת (byte tier), that form reaching 3 verses (sweep: 3 verses, MT 10:30, 12:6, 54:1). That is an in-span addressee shift contradicted rather than disclosed. Fourth, MT 12:5 is a ketiv/qere verse (one note), staged as the doubled pair מידעת מוּדַ֥עַת (oshb:Isa.12.5, byte tier), sitting inside the span and unchecked beneath the row's own count claim over that span. Two things verify: יָ֣הּ יְהוָ֔ה (oshb:Isa.12.2, byte tier) is rightly kept as its own short-form count-object, one of exactly 3 sites in the book (MT 12:2, 26:4, 38:11); and the petuchah at MT 12:6 is the correct type. The title closing the unit, קְד֥וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵֽל (oshb:Isa.12.6, byte tier), is cited only in English - and the plene spelling reaches 24 verses at skeleton tier while the title object is 25, the defective spelling at MT 49:7 being exactly what a plene-only needle misses.

items.claim: Keeping the verse-initial burden header with its Babylon oracle is right on the bytes, but the ground given for refusing a stand-alone header row does not separate this header from the other relative-clause superscription, the span's closing verse is quoted across an undisclosed ketiv/qere note, and the first-person divine voice the back-boundary argument treats as new is already running inside the span.
items.evidence: The header verifies: מַשָּׂ֖א בָּבֶ֑ל אֲשֶׁ֣ר חָזָ֔ה יְשַׁעְיָ֖הוּ בֶּן אָמֽוֹץ (oshb:Isa.13.1, byte tier), with the burden-noun as the verse's first token; the burden skeleton reaches 15 verses in the book, of which 10 are verse-initial oracle headers and the remainder are the mid-verse header reference and the burden-noun sites, and this one is verse-initial - correctly kept with the oracle it opens rather than set apart. But the stated ground, grammatical fusion to the content it opens, does not separate MT 13:1 from MT 2:1, which the frame architecture does treat as a stand-alone header: MT 2:1 is הַדָּבָר֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר חָזָ֔ה יְשַֽׁעְיָ֖הוּ בֶּן אָמ֑וֹץ (byte tier) and MT 13:1 is מַשָּׂ֖א בָּבֶ֑ל אֲשֶׁ֣ר חָזָ֔ה יְשַׁעְיָ֖הוּ בֶּן אָמֽוֹץ (byte tier), and the relative clause is BYTE-IDENTICAL in both - אֲשֶׁ֣ר חָזָ֔ה at MT 2:1 and אֲשֶׁ֣ר חָזָ֔ה at MT 13:1 - with the verbal see-plus-prophet pairing reaching exactly 2 verses (sweep: 2 verses, MT 2:1 and 13:1). Both are a nominal head plus that same relative clause; the byte feature that does separate them is that Babylon is bound to the burden-noun in construct while the other header attaches its target with a preposition after the patronymic - not the ground the row states. Next, MT 13:16 is a ketiv/qere verse (one note), staged as the doubled pair inside וּנְשֵׁיהֶ֖ם תשגלנה תִּשָּׁכַֽבְנָה (oshb:Isa.13.16, byte tier); it is the row's own closing verse and the English clause quoted for that boundary renders the qere, yet no apparatus disclosure is made. Finally, the back-boundary argument calls the following verse a distinct divine first-person onset, but first-person divine speech is already live inside the span at MT 13:3, אֲנִ֥י צִוֵּ֖יתִי (byte tier; sweep: 1 verse), and MT 13:11, וּפָקַדְתִּ֤י (byte tier; sweep: 1 verse), and a presentative already stands at MT 13:9, הִנֵּ֤ה יוֹם יְהוָה֙ (byte tier); the byte feature actually distinctive at the seam is the first-person suffix on the presentative, not 'behold' and not first person as such. Parashah verifies: petuchah at MT 12:6, correct type, and no petuchah or setumah inside MT 13:1-16, so no symmetry debt (absence is never counterevidence); one paseq seg stands at MT 13:8 (single-witness, count-only). One register note: the rationale narrates governance authority for the header ruling instead of stating the ground by content.

items.claim: The onset is byte-sound, verse-initial and genuinely distinctive, but a catchword attested in exactly two verses of the book straddles this row's front seam undisclosed, and the near-time predication brackets the whole burden across the same cut.
items.evidence: The onset verifies: הִנְנִ֛י is the first token of MT 13:17 and the quoted run הִנְנִ֛י מֵעִ֥יר עֲלֵיהֶ֖ם אֶת מָדָ֑י matches the source bytes at byte tier; the first-person-suffixed presentative reaches 14 verses book-wide at skeleton tier and MT 13:17 is its only site in this oracle, so it is a real signal and properly distinct from the plain presentative at MT 13:9. The named instrument אֶת מָדָ֑י (oshb:Isa.13.17, byte tier) is genuinely new to the oracle, and it is quoted rather than swept because its bare skeleton is a short-token trap that matches many unrelated words. The back seam is right: the next verse opens כִּי֩ יְרַחֵ֨ם יְהוָ֜ה (oshb:Isa.14.1, byte tier), a causal clause with a new addressee. What is missing is the front-seam disclosure. The shatter-root is attested in exactly 2 verses in this book (sweep: 2 verses, MT 13:16 and 13:18) - וְעֹלְלֵיהֶ֥ם יְרֻטְּשׁ֖וּ (oshb:Isa.13.16, byte tier) on the far side of the cut and וּקְשָׁת֖וֹת נְעָרִ֣ים תְּרַטַּ֑שְׁנָה (oshb:Isa.13.18, byte tier) on this side; the two forms are not byte-identical to each other (different stems), so the recurrence is skeleton-tier, but a two-site catchword falling on both sides of an oracle-internal join argues continuity across the cut unless disclosed, and neither side of the seam discloses it. The oracle is bracketed across the same cut as well: כִּ֥י קָר֖וֹב at MT 13:6 opens the day-of-Yahweh call and וְקָר֤וֹב לָבוֹא֙ at MT 13:22 closes the burden's last line (that skeleton reaches 8 verses, MT keys Isa.13.6, 13:22, 33:13, 50:8, 51:5, 55:6, 56:1, 57:19), so this row's closing verse answers a verse sitting inside the preceding unit. Apparatus and mark layers are clean and correctly left unclaimed: no petuchah or setumah and no ketiv/qere note inside MT 13:17-22, the next mark being a setumah at MT 14:2 outside the span; retaining the header-bounded value without a fresh header is correct. One near-miss that is NOT a defect: the gazelle simile at MT 13:14 and the glory-noun at MT 13:19 share a skeleton across the cut, but they are a homograph pair, not a catchword.
